punchline: According to Buckingham and Clifton, the task that makes you lose track of time is the last clue to a talent, not the first.
thirty_sec: Donald Clifton and Marcus Buckingham define talent as a recurring pattern of thought, feeling or behavior that can be productively applied. An ability is only a strength if you can imagine doing it repeatedly, happily and successfully. They list clues in order: yearnings, rapid learning and, last, satisfactions. For that last one the test is whether you get so absorbed that you lose track of time.
